Hi Ben — great questions. I've pulled Soojin and Sean into this reply so they can cover the technical and contract sides on our call. Below are short answers and attachments; happy to expand on each on Tuesday.

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering
- VPC peering: establishes a direct route between VPCs (lower latency, fewer hops), but requires cross-account route management and is best when both sides can control route tables. Works well if Acme can accept cross-account peering and manage CIDR overlap.
- PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink): exposes an endpoint service in our account that you connect to via an ENI in your VPC. Simpler from a security boundary perspective (no route table changes required on your side), but can introduce an extra network hop and slightly higher egress costs. In practice, we see PrivateLink add ~5-20ms on top of peering for short-request workloads depending on AZ topology.

2) Egress IPs & allowlist
- Control plane: stable set of egress IPs (we provide a list for US regions). For Private VPC deployments we offer a small, SLA-backed set of NAT IPs for control plane traffic.
- Model downloads/updates: can be routed through your S3 endpoints or via Redwood-managed egress — we can support routing model syncs over a peered connection so downloads come from your NAT (no external egress).
- Inference endpoints: if you use PrivateLink, endpoints appear as interface endpoints in your VPC and do not require external egress. If you use peering, traffic stays within the peered network. We'll provide the specific IPs for the control plane and a CIDR range for any managed egress.

Action: Soojin will share the canonical allowlist file and the exact IPs for the US control plane prior to the call.

3) KMS integration
- Yes — we support customer-managed KMS keys for Private VPC and Dedicated deployments. We'll need a cross-account grant and the KMS key ARN. Soojin can walk through the steps on our technical call.

4) On-prem / air-gapped option
- Redwood offers an on-prem package as a special enterprise engagement. It includes an air-gapped runtime bundle, offline licensing, and local key management. Recommend we treat this as a separate track — we can scope with your security team after the initial Private VPC deployment.
